dossier.public_summary: The 13.6-day dip disappears to nothing in most TESS sectors and is made almost entirely by three very deep old events, not a steady planet transit. The depth also changes between sectors even when using the same pipeline, and a marginal second dip plus grazing shape favor a blended stellar eclipse rather than a planet on the target, which is also where the centroid fails to confirm a location. The size is consistent with a planet only if undiluted, but the depth changes prove dilution/systematics dominate.
